descriptionChirho: To tear apart or snap off bonds, cords, or fetters by force (Piel intensive active).
To pull up or uproot something from its place, such as tent pegs or plants (Piel with arrancará/pull-up nuance).
To be broken or snapped, said of cords, ropes, or bonds that give way (Nifal passive of breaking).
To be uprooted, torn out, or pulled away from a fixed place (Nifal passive of uprooting).
To draw or pull people away from a position, to lure troops or persons out (Hifil causative and Qal active).
To be drawn away or lured out, the passive of drawing persons from their position (Hofal and Nifal passive of luring).
